prompt_c2:
You are a streetscape inventory annotator. Look ONLY at the uploaded streetscape image.
Return JSON ONLY. No markdown, no commentary, no reasoning.
 Task: record what is visible in the scene. Do not score, do not give design advice.
 Schema:
{
"road_type": "highway|arterial|neighborhood_street|alley|plaza|unclear",
"elements": {
"sidewalk": "true|false|unclear",
"bike_lane": "true|false|unclear",
"seating": "true|false|unclear",
"shade_trees": "none|few|many|unclear",
"curb_ramp": "true|false|unclear",
"tactile_paving": "true|false|unclear",
"pedestrian_crossing": "true|false|unclear",
"street_lighting": "true|false|unclear",
"greenery": "none|low|medium|high|unclear",
"vehicle_traffic": "none|light|heavy|unclear",
"bus_stop": "true|false|unclear"
},
"issues": ["no_seating", "little_shade", "no_bike_lane", "poor_accessibility", "narrow_sidewalk", "no_crossing", "high_traffic_exposure"],
"brief": "One or two English sentences describing the visible street scene."
}
 Rules:
- If an element is not clearly visible, use "unclear". Do not guess.
- "issues" may only list problems that are visible. Use [] if none.
- "brief" must mention concrete objects (sidewalk, trees, lanes, benches, ramps, etc.).

On road sections marked with parking spaces, motor vehicles shall be parked within the parking spaces in the direction of travel or in the direction indicated, and shall not be parked across parking spaces or parked continuously beyond the prescribed time limit. At night when there is no street lighting, or under meteorological conditions of low visibility such as wind, snow, rain, or fog, when a motor vehicle is temporarily parked on a road outside a parking lot, it shall, in addition to complying with the preceding paragraph, also switch on the hazard warning flashers, position lamps, and rear position lamps. **Article 57** Non-motor vehicles shall be parked at designated locations. Where no parking location is provided, the parking of non-motor vehicles shall not obstruct the passage of other vehicles or pedestrians. **Article 58** It is prohibited to drive livestock on urban roads and expressways. When walking with pets on the road, they shall be led on foot and properly supervised. **Article 59** Road testing, demonstration application, access and registration, and use management of conditionally automated vehicles, highly automated vehicles, and fully automated vehicles shall be implemented in accordance with relevant national and provincial provisions. Conditionally automated vehicles and highly automated vehicles shall be equipped with a driver when traveling on the road. Paths and paved areas in roadside green spaces shall meet the following requirements: 1. The material and thickness of the paving surface layer shall be coordinated with the road greening style and use function, and integrated with sponge city design. Ecological permeable materials should be used where possible, with anti-slip functions, and polished surface materials shall not be used. 2. Paved areas should have shading measures, and the shaded area in summer should preferably be greater than 50% of the recreational activity area. 1.4.1 Paving Style and Color 1. Quality improvement of non-motorized vehicle lane paving In riverside greenways and other leisure spaces, or at locations with a significantly high incidence of traffic accidents involving motor vehicles and non-motorized vehicles, non-motorized vehicle lanes may use colored paving. Isolation facilities may be appropriately arranged to improve the cycling experience for non-motorized vehicles. Figure 1.4-1 Schematic diagram of non-motorized vehicle lane paving 2. Quality improvement of sidewalk paving 11 A. Traffic-function roads The sides of traffic-function roads are mainly non-open interfaces, with relatively few non-traffic activities, and the paved areas mainly serve traffic distribution functions. Paving design shall implement the concepts of safety, health, comfort, and people-oriented design. Figure 1.4-2 Example of paving for traffic-function roads B. Living-service roads The activity groups on living-service roads include residents and workers around the road, as well as people from other areas who come for shopping and strolling. In terms of paving materials, color, texture, and grain, attention shall be paid to people’s perceptions, and localized creative design shall be applied to road entrances to enrich the walking experience. Figure 1.4-3 Example of paving for living-service roads C. Scenic leisure roads According to the characteristics of scenic leisure roads and the behavioral characteristics of the activity groups, the design objective of the paved area is to provide a safe, comfortable slow-traffic environment and leisure space. The paving surface layer shall use natural, aesthetically pleasing, comfortable, and ecological materials, while also meeting the requirement of coordination with the surrounding landscape. 12 Figure 1.4-4 Example of paving for scenic leisure roads D. Historic-style streets and lanes The paving design of historic-style streets and lanes shall continue and reflect cultural charm and local character, and shape distinctive spaces. Road design should focus on creating a historical and cultural atmosphere. The paving materials and texture shall be integrated with the surrounding environment. Figure 1.4-5 Example of paving for historic-style streets and lanes E. Comprehensive roads Comprehensive roads have a relatively high degree of mixing in road functions and interface types. They shall take into account the different needs of multiple characteristics, optimize the slow-traffic travel experience, consider the composite needs of road functions and the businesses on both sides, and create a paving system that is highly adaptable and simple and elegant. Figure 1.4-6 Example of paving for comprehensive roads F. Smart city demonstration roads No special requirements

As a city streetscape evaluation expert, please analyze the uploaded streetscape image based on the specified persona perspective and evaluation indicators, and return a JSON result.
 Persona Selection
Road User Type
- All Road Users
- Pedestrians
- Cyclists
- Drivers
Socially Vulnerable Groups
- All Social Groups

- Adolescents (<18)
- Older Adults (≥60)

- Accessibility

- Psychological Comfort

Selected Indicators:

 1. Evaluation Dimensions
Justice: Analyze whether the environment fairly distributes spatial resources, including Equity (rationality of asset distribution), Fairness (non-discriminatory rules), and Accessibility (barrier-free physical design).
Comfort: Analyze physical perception at a micro-scale, including Thermal Comfort (shade/vegetation), Physical Comfort (paving/seating), and Psychological Comfort (noise/crowding).
Core Indicators: Safety, Livability, Sustainability, Aesthetics, Walkability, and Bikeability.
 2. Persona Perspective Requirements:
The analysis must strictly adhere to the persona's characteristics. For example:
Persons with Disabilities: Focus on curb ramps, continuity of tactile paving (blind tracks), and physical obstacles.
Elderly: Focus on resting facilities, slope gradients, and summer shade.
Teenagers: Focus on traffic calming measures and social surveillance (Eyes on the street).
 3. How to use the image vs retrieved knowledge:
- The IMAGE is the primary evidence. Score only what is visible or reasonably inferable from the photo.
- Section 6 provides retrieved guidelines and research. Use them to interpret the image (what the scene should provide for this persona/indicators), not to invent objects that are not in the photo.
- If retrieved text conflicts with the image, trust the image and say so in the explanation.
- Explanations must cite specific visible objects (benches, ramps, tree shade, lane markings, etc.). When a guideline is used, briefly connect it to those objects.

The layout of intersection approach roads shall meet the following requirements: at intersections between arterial roads and secondary arterial roads, the number of through lanes on the approach road (including through-left or through-right lanes) shall not be less than the number of lanes on the road section. 3. The lanes on the exit road of an intersection shall match the maximum number of approach lanes flowing into the same signal phase from the upstream approaches. For reconstructed intersections with constrained conditions, the maximum number of inflow approach lanes may be reduced by one. Where adjacent approaches are provided with dedicated right-turn lanes, the exit road shall be widened by one dedicated right-turn exit

On road sections marked with parking spaces, motor vehicles shall be parked within the parking spaces in the direction of travel or in the direction indicated, and shall not be parked across parking spaces or parked continuously beyond the prescribed time limit. At night when there is no street lighting, or under meteorological conditions of low visibility such as wind, snow, rain, or fog, when a motor vehicle is temporarily parked on a road outside a parking lot, it shall, in addition to complying with the preceding paragraph, also switch on the hazard warning flashers, position lamps, and rear position lamps. **Article 57** Non-motor vehicles shall be parked at designated locations. Where no parking location is provided, the parking of non-motor vehicles shall not obstruct the passage of other vehicles or pedestrians. **Article 58** It is prohibited to drive livestock on urban roads and expressways. When walking with pets on the road, they shall be led on foot and properly supervised. **Article 59** Road testing, demonstration application, access and registration, and use management of conditionally automated vehicles, highly automated vehicles, and fully automated vehicles shall be implemented in accordance with relevant national and provincial provisions. Conditionally automated vehicles and highly automated vehicles shall be equipped with a driver when traveling on the road. The driver shall use the automated driving function in a standardized manner in accordance with road traffic rules and the vehicle’s user manual; when the automated driving function is activated, the driver shall be seated in the driver’s seat, monitor the vehicle’s operating status and surrounding environment, and when the vehicle issues a takeover request or is in a state unsuitable for automated driving, the driver shall immediately take over the vehicle. Paths and paved areas in roadside green spaces shall meet the following requirements: 1. The main stop is a bay stop, while the auxiliary stop is a direct stop where vehicles stop directly. 30 Figure 2.1-8 Schematic of a Double Bay Bus Stop 2.1.7 Roadside Parking Lane The general rules for parking space arrangement are as follows: 1. At unsignalized intersections where the approach or departure road is a single lane, no parking spaces shall be set within 10 m of the straight curb segment on the intersection approach side; no parking spaces shall be set within 8 m of the straight curb segment on the departure side. 2. At channelized intersections, no parking spaces shall be set within the channelized area and within 5 m outside it. 3. No parking spaces shall be set within 6 m on the departure side and 10 m on the approach side, measured from the starting point of the straight curb segment on both sides of a parcel entrance/exit. 4. No parking spaces shall be set within 8 m upstream and 6 m downstream of the vehicle stop line in the direction of approach to a pedestrian crossing. 5. No parking spaces shall be set within 25 m before and 15 m after a bus stop platform. 6. No parking spaces shall be set in the ground space corresponding to a radius of 1.5 m from the center of the manhole cover of underground utility access shafts. 7. The distance between parking spaces before and after a fire hydrant shall not be less than 30 m, and the distance from the nearest parking space to the fire hydrant shall not be less than 2.5 m.
